clue.text: For the setting, read the original words

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or read carefully
a text is the original wording of a work

explanation.surface: A scholar told to study the source to understand the background.
explanation.definitionFit: The context of something is its surrounding circumstances or background.

clue.text: Pilgrim moving a Swedish queen

indicators.note: moving says one letter of the pilgrim's name shifts to a new place

parts.note: Christian is the pilgrim hero of Bunyan's The Pilgrim's Progress

explanation.surface: A traveller on a pilgrimage meets Scandinavian royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: The A of CHRISTIAN moves to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Christina was the seventeenth-century queen of Sweden who abdicated and converted to Catholicism.

clue.text: Special cell in which time is' served-one's never charged

indicators.note: in which, with time is served, means a letter is put inside the cell

parts.note: a neuron is a specialised nerve cell

explanation.surface: A prison cell where a sentence is served by someone never charged with a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: The prison reading of cell, time and charged misleads; the charge is electric. 'is served' completes the container indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: A neutron is a subatomic particle with no electric charge.

clue.text: Delighted when gate is increased by 500

indicators.note: increased by means something is added on to the end

parts.note: a gate is an entrance
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: A football club is pleased when attendance rises by five hundred.
explanation.definitionFit: Entranced means enchanted or filled with wonder.

clue.text: Mealtime for feeding calves

parts.note: tea is an afternoon or evening meal

explanation.surface: Feeding time on the farm for young cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: A cow's nipple is how a calf suckles milk.

clue.text: Vulgar money that is on display in golf club

parts.note: brass is slang for money, often used of showy wealth
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A nouveau-riche golfer flashes cash at the clubhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A brassie is an old name for a wooden golf club, the number two wood.

clue.text: Artillery unit he found heading north — its range is very restricted

parts.note: a battery is a group of guns

explanation.surface: A gunner heads north, his firing range tightly limited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found heading' says HE comes before N. The range is free range, which a caged hen lacks.
explanation.definitionFit: A battery hen is kept in a small cage, unable to roam free.

clue.text: Protective covering for area where planes stand

definitions.meaning: the paved airport area where aircraft park

explanation.surface: A cover laid down where aircraft wait.
explanation.definitionFit: Apron names both a garment for shielding clothes and an airfield parking area.

clue.text: River's quiet soon broken by onset of noise

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet

indicators.note: broken by means one piece is split open with another put inside

parts.note: anon is an old word for soon

indicators.note: onset means the start, so the first letter of noise

explanation.surface: A peaceful river disturbed by a sudden din.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of River's stands for is, joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shannon is the longest river in Ireland.

clue.text: Spirit that's characteristic of those moving East

indicators.note: the letter for East shifts its place within the word those

explanation.surface: The mood typical of people migrating eastward.
explanation.walkthrough: The E of THOSE moves to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethos is the distinctive character or guiding spirit of a group or culture.

clue.text: Beginning to roll, drive out and get on the move

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, taken here from roll

parts.note: to oust is to drive out or expel

explanation.surface: A command to start rolling and hustle people out.
explanation.definitionFit: To roust is to rouse someone and make them stir into action.

clue.text: Consequences following certain problems in US school

parts.note: after means following
Americans call mathematics math rather than maths

explanation.surface: Struggling with sums at an American school has its consequences.
explanation.definitionFit: An aftermath is the set of results that follow an event, usually a bad one.

clue.text: Second best -what a joke!

parts.note: the cream is the best part of anything

explanation.surface: Someone finishing runner-up laughs it off.
explanation.definitionFit: A scream is informal for something or someone hilariously funny.

clue.text: Range of England's artillery initially less than Italian range

indicators.note: less means without, so a letter is taken away from the Italian range

parts.note: the Apennines are the mountain chain running down Italy

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of artillery

explanation.surface: England's mountains, as a firing range, fall short of Italy's.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pennines are the chain of hills forming the backbone of northern England.

clue.text: I can produce PR cons, and do it to order

definitions.text: I can produce PR cons, and do it to order

indicators.note: to order means arranged afresh, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A publicist boasts of conjuring public-relations tricks on demand.
explanation.definitionFit: A spin doctor is a political press officer who puts a favourable slant on news.

clue.text: Perversely funny, having lost right order

indicators.note: having lost means a letter is dropped from the word for perversely funny

parts.note: ironic humour is funny in a contrary, perverse way

explanation.surface: A comedian whose humour has stopped being funny loses the right to command.
explanation.definitionFit: Ionic is one of the classical orders of architecture, with scroll-shaped capitals.

clue.text: Happy to change individual's costly communication devices

indicators.note: to change asks for the letters to be rearranged

parts.note: one is an individual, so one's stands for individual's

explanation.surface: A cheerful person switches to someone else's expensive gadgets.
explanation.definitionFit: Payphones are public telephones that charge for each call, so using one costs money.

clue.text: What's there for their house to clean and sharpen?

parts.note: to mop is to clean
to hone is to sharpen

explanation.surface: A cleaner wonders what tools their household needs for scrubbing and sharpening.
explanation.definitionFit: Words that sound alike but differ in spelling, like there and their, are this kind of word.

clue.text: Firm dates arranged with expedition

indicators.note: arranged means put into a new order, so the letters are reshuffled

parts.note: expedition means speed, so with expedition is quickly or fast

explanation.surface: Dates are fixed quickly and firmly.
explanation.definitionFit: Steadfast means resolutely firm and unwavering.

clue.text: What will happen, we hear, in this part of grammar

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is said aloud rather than spelt

parts.note: accidents will happen, as the proverb has it

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson warns that mishaps are inevitable.
explanation.definitionFit: Accidence is the branch of grammar dealing with inflections of words.

clue.text: Took a risk — part of church finally increased tenfold

indicators.note: the last letter, a Roman fifty, becomes the Roman numeral ten times bigger

parts.note: the chancel is the part of a church near the altar

explanation.surface: Gambling on a church extension ten times larger.
explanation.walkthrough: L is Roman 50; multiplied by ten it becomes D, Roman 500.
explanation.definitionFit: Chanced means ventured or gambled.

clue.text: Man drinking quietly in wood

indicators.note: drinking means taking something in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a man is a male
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A fellow sipping a drink quietly in the forest.
explanation.definitionFit: Maple is a hardwood timber prized for furniture and flooring.

clue.text: Get excited after taking pawn, rook, and bishop?

indicators.note: after taking means the excitement comes after the chess pieces

parts.note: P is the chess notation for pawn
R is the chess notation for rook
to elate is to make jubilant

explanation.surface: A chess player thrills at capturing pawn, rook and bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess setting misleads: bishop is a churchman, not a piece; the question mark flags the example.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop is one example of a senior churchman.

clue.text: Pulling power of a medical treatment

definitions.meaning: the grip or pulling force of a vehicle or engine
the use of weights and pulleys to stretch a limb or spine

explanation.surface: An engine's pull applied as a hospital remedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Traction is both the force of pulling and an orthopaedic stretching treatment.

clue.text: Pack to go to a resort in Florida

parts.note: to tamp is to pack down firmly

explanation.surface: Packing up for a holiday at a Florida beach town.
explanation.definitionFit: Tampa is a city on Florida's Gulf coast popular with holidaymakers.

clue.text: Nothing's gained in cutting such a card

indicators.note: gained in means put inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: tart means sharp or cutting, as of a remark
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A card player cuts the deck and wins nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarot card belongs to a deck used in fortune-telling.

clue.text: Elaborate meal producing increased girth

definitions.meaning: middle-age ... is the thickening waistline that comes with age

explanation.surface: A lavish feast that leaves one wider round the waist.
explanation.definitionFit: A spread is both a feast laid out and, informally, a widening of the body.

clue.text: Landed gentry have such an advantage

indicators.note: have means the words contain the answer inside them

explanation.surface: Aristocrats with estates enjoy a head start.
explanation.definitionFit: An edge is a slight advantage over others.

clue.text: Club considered to have turned soft

parts.note: a mace is a heavy club used as a weapon
rated means considered or judged

explanation.surface: A golf club deemed to have lost its toughness.
explanation.definitionFit: Macerated food has been softened by soaking in liquid.

clue.text: Honour met with a derisive expression in American city

parts.note: the OM, or Order of Merit, is a British honour
aha is an exclamation of mocking triumph

explanation.surface: A decorated dignitary is jeered on a trip to the States.
explanation.definitionFit: Omaha is the largest city in Nebraska.

clue.text: Listener paying close attention to account

definitions.meaning: a hearer, from Latin audire to hear

explanation.surface: Someone who hears out a story while checking the books.
explanation.definitionFit: An auditor is literally a hearer and professionally an inspector of accounts.

clue.text: High point of holiday taken by First Lady

parts.note: Eve was the first woman in the Bible
a rest is a break or holiday

explanation.surface: The President's wife takes a vacation at a peak.
explanation.definitionFit: Everest is the world's highest mountain, and so a byword for a summit.
